summary: Visibility-only refactor is correct and minimal. The four targeted members (requireValidTokenShape, isTransient, DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT, CONNECT_TIMEOUT) are widened from private static to public static; bodies, signatures, parameter names, return types, and constant values are byte-identical to the pre-commit version. The other private members called out in the task (MONO_TIMEOUT, CAUSE_CHAIN_MAX_HOPS, TOKEN_PATTERN, TOKEN_SHAPE) remain private as required. The four new promotion comments follow the existing scrubTokens precedent verbatim in tone and shape (two-line // block, starts with 'Promoted to public for shared use by …', em-dash, factual rationale; no Javadoc drift). A repo-wide grep for the four members confirms no external consumer exists today outside TelegramApiClient itself and its test, so the widening is recompile-clean and has zero ripple. The existing TelegramApiClientTest suite remains green (gradlew test --tests TelegramApiClientTest reported BUILD SUCCESSFUL with all tasks up-to-date), and the commit diff touches only the four expected lines (12 insertions / 4 deletions) in the single expected file. No critical or major findings; no blocking concerns. Acceptance criteria for Task 1 / Decision 12 / user-spec AC5 + R2 are fully satisfied.

findings.title: DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT and MONO_TIMEOUT share the same 10s value but only one is promoted, with no in-file note explaining the asymmetry
findings.detail: DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT (10s, the TCP read timeout on the HttpClient) is now public; MONO_TIMEOUT (10s, the outer reactive .timeout(...) on each getMe/setWebhook/deleteWebhook call) stays private. The two constants have the same numeric value and adjacent declaration lines, which can read as 'one was forgotten' to a reader who does not have tech-spec Decision 12 in front of them. Decision 12 and the task description both spell out the rationale (TelegramSender has its own outer 30s timeout — Decision 8 — so MONO_TIMEOUT must NOT be shared), but the file itself is silent on why the two adjacent 10s constants split visibility. The promotion comments on DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT and CONNECT_TIMEOUT explain why they were widened; nothing on MONO_TIMEOUT explains why it was deliberately kept private. A future maintainer doing a similar promotion (Task 4's TelegramSender bean, or a later sender) might assume MONO_TIMEOUT is a follow-up omission rather than an intentional boundary, and widen it 'for consistency' — which would silently couple the connect-flow's response-Mono timeout to whichever sender reads it.
findings.suggestion: Optional follow-up (not blocking for this task; the spec's intent is documented in tech-spec Decision 12 and Decision 8): add a one-line // comment above MONO_TIMEOUT noting 'kept private — connect-flow's per-call outer reactive timeout; senders define their own outer timeout (TelegramSender uses 30s per Decision 8) and must not reuse this value.' This mirrors the explanatory-comment habit established by scrubTokens / the four promotions and pre-empts a future accidental widening. Defer to Task 4 if you'd rather only land it once a second consumer concretely exists.
